rationale: dual_domain_supervised-claude-agentic: unet_c=16, epochs=44, batch_size=2, lr=0.001, optimizer=adam, lambda_neg=0.03, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=400, val_n=200, val_chunk=10, seed=42, rationale=iter-13 dual_domain_supervised, re-split Breast-CT val=200. SIX-BOX vs BEST (iter-8 c16/ep44/lr1e-3/lneg0.03/bs1/tn400 hr=0.8915). (1) PRIOR: lr BRACKETED -- 5e-4<1e-3(best)>2e-3 (iter-12=0.8470, sharp drop). epochs SATURATE ~44 (iter-11 ep52 flat). VERIFIED the solver hardcodes Adam(lr) with NO lr_schedule/weight_decay/AdamW support, so those are NOT available knobs. Remaining effective config knobs: batch_size, train_n, seed. (2) Failure mode: constant lr=1e-3 with batch_size=1 gives noisy single-sample gradients that may jitter near the minimum instead of settling. (3) ONE KNOB: batch_size 1 -> 2 (iter-8 config otherwise identical). Breast has NO per-sample-ps constraint (_per_ps=False), so batching >1 is valid here (unlike Mayo). (4) HYPOTHESIS: batch_size=2 averages 2 samples/step -> smoother gradients settle into a marginally better minimum -> hr >= 0.8915, and it is also ~faster (half the steps) so budget-safe. If hr DROPS, single-sample stochasticity was beneficial and iter-14 reverts to bs=1 and tries a modest train_n bump (400->500) at ep=44. Expect ~0.89-0.895. (5) BUDGET: <= iter-8 941s (fewer optimizer steps), inside 20-min budget. (6) Loop to iter-20. Artifacts saved.
